findings.title: Tier 3 falls back to first allowed model instead of raising
findings.problem: _pick_from_override returns override.default_model or project default or override.allowed_models[0]. Spec 3.5 tier 3 says use the override default, else Application.default_model, and raise ModelNotWhitelistedException if neither is set. The code never raises in this case, in both the sync resolver and resolve_model_for_execution_with_user_context.
findings.impact: When an override has no default_model and the project has no default, a requested model outside the override and project whitelist silently resolves to the first allowed model instead of failing as specified. Behavior differs from the approved spec; whether the graceful fallback is intended needs human intent.
findings.recommendation: Decide intent: keep the fallback and amend spec 3.5 tier 3, or raise ModelNotWhitelistedException when neither override nor project default is set.
